test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

She said, "Ruhi slipped when she was trying to board the bus."

options.text: She said that Ruhi had slipped when she was trying to board the bus.
She says that Ruhi slipped when she was trying to board the bus.
She said that Ruhi has slipped when she was trying to board the bus.
She said that Ruhi slipped when she was trying to board the bus.

solution:
The correct answer is **"She said that Ruhi slipped when she was trying to board the bus."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **
 

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a direct speech.**
 
• Rules to change these sentences:
 
 
• In these types of questions, the comma (,") is replaced with 'that'. 
 
• If the **past continuous tense/ simple past tense** is used within **a time clause (when)**, the **tense will remain the same** when the statement is converted from direct to indirect speech.
 
 
• For instance, if someone said, "*When I met him, he was playing,*" it would be reported as "*He said that when he met him, he was playing."*
 
• Hence, If one clause is in **past simple tense and the other is in past continuous, **they maintain their tenses when the speech is reported indirectly, especially with time clauses like 'when'. This principle is true regardless of whether the verb in the main clause is past simple or continuous.
 
• He said to me, “While I was studying, you were playing.” it would be reported as - He told me that while he was studying, I was playing.
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech with the simple past tense (slipped), as per the rule mentioned above, the tense will be unchanged.
 
• **'Said' will not get replaced with 'told'** as there is** no object** in the sentence.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct sentence: __*She said that Ruhi slipped when she was trying to board the bus.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 

 

 
• Simple past tense: A tense that is used to express an action that happened in the past, finished in past, and has no relation to the present or future.

 
 
• Example: She **went **to school in 1995.
 
 
 
• Past perfect sentence: The past perfect, sometimes referred to as the pluperfect, is a verb tense used to discuss activities that were carried out before a specific moment in time.
 
 
• Example: Prateek **had gone** out when I arrived at the office.
 
 
 
• Direct Speech: A direct speech reports the precise words used by a speaker or writer.
 
• Indirect Speech: Indirect speech focuses more on the content of what someone said rather than their exact words.
